title: Static vs Dynamic Polymorphism & Design Patterns

slides.title: Dynamic vs Static Polymorphism
slides.prompt: Dynamic polymorphism uses Virtual Tables at runtime. Static polymorphism uses Templates (CRTP) at compile-time with zero runtime overhead.

slides.title: CRTP Acronym
slides.prompt: CRTP stands for Curiously ___ Template Pattern.

slides.title: Static Polymorphism Advantage
slides.prompt: What is the key performance benefit of CRTP / Static Polymorphism over Virtual Functions?
options: Zero runtime VTable lookup overhead and enables full compiler inlining
Reduces template code bloat in compiled binary
slides.correctAnswer: Zero runtime VTable lookup overhead and enables full compiler inlining

slides.title: Dynamic Polymorphism Unique Capability
slides.prompt: Which capability is exclusive to Dynamic Polymorphism that Static Polymorphism cannot do directly?
options: Storing different derived types dynamically in a single container at runtime
slides.correctAnswer: Storing different derived types dynamically in a single container at runtime

slides.title: Non-Virtual Interface (NVI) Idiom
slides.prompt: NVI Idiom calls private virtual methods inside a ___ public base method.
slides.codeSnippet:
// Public NVI wrapper method is:
NonVirtual

slides.title: NVI Idiom Advantage
slides.prompt: Why use the Non-Virtual Interface (NVI) pattern in class design?
options: Allows Base class to control pre-conditions and post-conditions before calling virtual implementation
Eliminates the requirement for virtual destructors
Converts dynamic polymorphism into static polymorphism
slides.correctAnswer: Allows Base class to control pre-conditions and post-conditions before calling virtual implementation

slides.title: Strategy Pattern Variant
slides.prompt: How can Strategy Pattern be implemented without VTable runtime overhead in Modern C++?
options: Using template policy parameters or std::variant with std::visit
Using multiple inheritance of concrete classes
Using raw void pointers and function pointer offsets
slides.correctAnswer: Using template policy parameters or std::variant with std::visit
